title: Austin City Limits Music Festival (25th Anniversary)
description: The big one, y'all. Two weekends of Zilker turning into a nine-stage sea of humanity for ACL's 25th go-round, with Charli XCX, Twenty One Pilots, Lorde, RUFUS DU SOL and the whole tribe. Wear sunscreen, pace yourself in the food-truck line, and let the live oaks do the shade work. This is Austin showing off, no pretension required.
pin_ticker: ACL Fest 25th anniversary - Zilker, both weekends
admission: Ticketed - weekend passes and single-day tickets via aclfestival.com

title: Formula 1 United States Grand Prix
address: 9201 Circuit of the Americas Blvd, Austin, TX 78617
description: Three days of screaming engines out at COTA, capped by the Grand Prix itself Sunday at 2. Practice and support races Friday, qualifying Saturday, and headline concerts each night (Maroon 5, Post Malone at Germania). Even if you don't know a chicane from a chalupa, the energy is electric and the people-watching is a sport of its own.
pin_ticker: F1 US Grand Prix - race Sunday 2PM at COTA
admission: Ticketed - 3-day and single-day passes via circuitoftheamericas.com

title: Austin Trail of Lights
description: Sixty-plus years running and still the coziest way to spend a December night in town. Two million lights strung through Zilker, the spinning Zilker Tree to make yourself dizzy under, food trucks, Santa photos, and rides for the kids. Free general admission on select early nights - come those nights, tip a hot cocoa, and keep it merry and weird.
pin_ticker: Trail of Lights - Zilker, nightly 7-10PM, free early nights
admission: Free general admission Dec 10-12 & 15-18; ticketed on other nights

title: Austin Bat Fest
location: Ann W. Richards Congress Avenue Bridge
description: Only festival in Austin that happens on a bridge, over the largest urban bat colony in North America. Live music, food, and bat-themed everything while you wait for 1.5 million Mexican free-tailed bats to pour out at dusk. Peak keep-it-weird. Bring patience and look up.
pin_ticker: Bat Fest - live music on Congress Bridge + the bat emergence
_source: https://10times.com/annual-bat-fest and roadwayevents.com - Sep 2026 (Sep 5 per listings, confirm exact date)

title: LEVITATION Festival
location: Red River Cultural District & East Side venues
description: Four nights of psych rock, punk, darkwave and everything in the genre-bending in-between, spread across Stubb's, Mohawk, Empire, Hotel Vegas and the Red River clubs with Radio/East as the hub. This is Austin's underground turned all the way up - late-night shows, sweat, and a lineup that rewards the curious.
pin_ticker: LEVITATION - psych/punk across Red River & East Side clubs
admission: Ticketed - festival passes and single shows via levitation.fm

title: Fantastic Fest (20th Edition)
description: The largest genre film festival in the U.S. - horror, sci-fi, action and the gloriously strange - turning 20 at the Alamo Drafthouse on South Lamar. Premieres, filmmaker Q&As, and the kind of midnight-movie crowd that cheers at the screen. Order a pitcher, settle in, and let it get weird in the best way.
pin_ticker: Fantastic Fest 20th - genre cinema at Alamo South Lamar
admission: Ticketed - badges and individual tickets via fantasticfest.com
_source: https://fantasticfest.com/ - Sep 17-24, 2026 at Alamo Drafthouse South Lamar

title: Viva la Vida Festival & Parade (43rd Annual)
description: Austin's largest and longest-running Dia de los Muertos celebration, hosted by the Mexic-Arte Museum. A Grand Procession kicks it off at noon on Congress, then hands-on art, altars, lowrider exhibition, traditional food and live performance. Free, joyful, and rooted deep in this city's Mexican-American heart.
pin_ticker: Viva la Vida - Austin's biggest Dia de los Muertos parade & fest

title: Austin Film Festival (33rd Annual)
description: The Writers' Festival - eight days where screenwriters are the stars, with panels, premieres and the famous conference where working writers actually talk shop. Screenings across downtown, badge-holders elbow to elbow with the people who make the movies. Come for the films, stay for the stories about the stories.
pin_ticker: Austin Film Festival - the Writers' Festival, downtown
admission: Ticketed - badges and film passes via austinfilmfestival.com

title: Wurstfest - New Braunfels (side trip)
description: A ten-day salute to sausage about 45 minutes south in New Braunfels - German beer, oompah bands, folk dancing, and more links than you can shake a fork at. A worthy Hill Country day trip if you want lederhosen with your Lone Star State. Pace yourself; the polka doesn't stop.
pin_ticker: Wurstfest - 10-day sausage & German beer fest, New Braunfels

title: Texas Book Festival
description: Bookworms take the Capitol - author talks, panels and tents lining 11th Street and Congress for one of the country's great literary weekends. Free to browse, with hundreds of authors and a cookbook stage that smells better than most. Grab a taco, find a shady seat, and let a stranger's book recommendation change your month.
pin_ticker: Texas Book Festival - authors & tents at the Capitol
admission: Free general admission; some ticketed sessions
_source: https://texasbookfestival.org/festival/ - Nov 14-15, 2026 at the Texas Capitol

title: Ascension Seton Austin Marathon, Half & 5K
address: Congress Ave & Cesar Chavez, Austin, TX 78701
description: Valentine's morning, the whole city laces up. Marathon, half and 5K rolling through downtown and the hills with live bands on the course and cowbell-ringing neighbors keeping you honest on those Austin inclines. Whether you're running it or cheering it, this is the town at its most warm-hearted.
pin_ticker: Austin Marathon - marathon, half & 5K through downtown
admission: Registration required via youraustinmarathon.com; free to spectate

title: SFC Farmers' Market Downtown
description: Every Saturday morning, rain or shine, Republic Square fills with 75-plus vendors - farm produce, pasture-raised meats, artisan bites and live music under the Auction Oak. Bring a tote and an appetite; this is where Austin does its weekend grocery run and runs into everybody it knows.
pin_ticker: SFC Farmers' Market - Saturdays 9-1 at Republic Square

title: Drop-In Summer Concert Series at the Long Center
location: The Long Center for the Performing Arts
description: Free live music every Thursday on the Long Center lawn with that unbeatable downtown-skyline-over-Lady-Bird-Lake backdrop. A rotating cast of Austin artists from country and pop to R&B and acid punk. Pack a blanket, catch the breeze off the water, and let summer be easy for once.
pin_ticker: Free Thursday concerts at the Long Center through Aug 13
_source: https://www.austintexas.org/events/june-and-july/ - Drop-In Summer Concert Series, Thursdays through Aug 13; confirm weekly lineup
